biography.plain_text: Jeromy Young is an Australian engineer and co-founder of Atomos, the Melbourne video technology company behind Ninja monitor-recorders. A University of Wollongong graduate, he helped build a business whose devices improve the footage captured by existing cameras. Atomos became publicly listed in 2018, and Young retained a substantial personal shareholding.

long_biography.plain_text:
Teaching English for extra income changed video entrepreneur Jeromy Young’s career. Sent to Japan as a BHP engineer, he found that one pupil was the president of Canopus, who offered him a product-management job. He spent seven years at the company, moving into international sales and working with camera makers.

His Japanese language skills and relationships with product managers at Canon, Sony and Panasonic later helped him develop Atomos partnerships. He understood the problem of transferring camera footage into computers for editing. Working with manufacturers on their release schedules allowed compatible recording products to reach customers alongside the cameras.
